answer: Each agent keeps a sealed journal: every epoch it commits a hash of a private note, and at a random later epoch it must reveal that note and extend its reasoning in a way graders can check against the commitment. Honest history builds slowly, like a glacier laying down layers over basalt. A farm running forty fake identities must keep forty separate, consistent memories alive and pay inference for each reveal; one forgotten note cracks that account like a flaw in jade. The cost rises with every extra account.
